The University of Sri Jayewardenepura is one of the oldest Universities in Sri Lanka. The origin of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura dates back to 1873, when Ven. Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala Nayaka Thero laid the foundation stone for the Vidyodaya (meaning “awakening of knowledge”) Pirivena. Vidyodaya Pirivena was granted University status in 1959, and the name was changed to ‘Vidyodaya University of Ceylon’. In 1961, the University was relocated from Maligakanda to a beautiful setting at Gangodawila, Nugegoda, in the outskirts of Colombo. Later, in 1978, the name of this higher educational institution was changed to ‘University of Sri Jayewardenepura’ and was granted an autonomous University status. 06

The University of Sri Jayewardenepura derives its authority from the Universities Act No. 16 of 1978 as amended. As one of the Universities established under the University Grants Commission, the University is empowered to confer degrees on persons who have duly registered to follow a programme of study and have satisfactorily completed all the requirements in conformity with the By-laws of the University as applicable to the Faculty of Engineering. Vice Chancellor is the Chief Executive and Principal Academic Officer of the University while the Deans of Faculties, Registrar, Librarian and the Bursar are recognized as Officers of the University. The Council, Senate and Faculty Board of each Faculty are recognized as authorities of the University. Council is the governing authority of the University whereas the Senate is the highest academic body. Faculty Boards are responsible for conducting study programmes under the directions of the Senate. The University of Sri Jayewardenepura consists of eleven Faculties, namely; Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Faculty of Applied Sciences, Faculty of Management Studies and Commerce, Faculty of Medical Sciences, Faculty of Graduate Studies, Faculty of Technology, Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, Faculty of Dental Sciences, Faculty of Computing and Faculty of Aquatic Bio-resources. The University commits itself for the pursuit and transmission of knowledge through teaching, scholarship, and research. It aims to serve the community through producing well-rounded graduates with creativity, freedom of intellectual thought and expression, and professional growth through nourishing an environment of equal opportunity and fairness. In addition, University of Sri Jayewardenepura plays an active role in conducting research in areas of national relevance such as Dengue, Cancer, Kidney and Water quality. All these activities are accomplished with the dedication of academic members and the support extended by the administrative divisions such as academic and non-academic establishment, general administration, finance, examinations, and student welfare.

The Faculty of Engineering, University of Sri Jayewardenepura, is the latest addition to the faculties of engineering in the state universities coming under the purview of the university grants commission. Established in January 2016, it consists of five departments of study with a mandate to offer study programmes in engineering, and in particular an undergraduate study programme in engineering leading to the award of the degree of the ‘Bachelor of the Science of Engineering’. The government in its budget speeches of 2014 and 2015, made provisions to establish a faculty of engineering and technology in the university of Sri Jayewardenepura. This is in-line with the national requirement for professionals to drive the country towards a knowledge-based economy. Following the government initiative, the then vice chancellor of the university, senior professor Sampath Amaratunge appointed an advisory board consisting of renowned personalities to proceed with modalities in establishing the new faculty. This advisory board comprised of professors, D.A.Tantrigoda, M.M.Karunanayake, A.M.Abeysekara, K.Deheragoda, P.B.Mandawala and the Emeritus professor N.R.Arthenayake who was a former vice chancellor of the open university of Sri Lanka (OUSL) ,former dean of the faculty of engineering technology of the OUSL and a senior professor in mechanical engineering was appointed as the lead consultant to shoulder the task of establishing the faculty of engineering and technology.

After extensive deliberations with regard to the differences in Technology and Engineering streams as well as the difference in the admission criteria applicable to respective study programmes together with prevailing practicalities, then Vice Chancellor proposed to establish two new Faculties, namely, Faculty of Engineering and Faculty of Technology. This decision was approved by the Senate and the Council of the University. Four Senior Lecturers, namely Dr.S.A.A.M. Subasinghe, Dr.C.de Alwis, Dr. M. Mohomed, and Dr. K.M.C. Konthesingha, were recruited to the proposed Faculty of Engineering to be engaged in the task of developing an Engineering Degree Programme, under the guidance of Professor Arthenayake. A Consultative Committee in Engineering (CCE) consisting of eminent academics in Engineering Education in the country, together with the representation of the Institution of Engineers, Sri Lanka (IESL) were appointed to spearhead the development of the Engineering Degree Programme. Leading industrialists in the country were consulted to incorporate their inputs to the curriculum development process and the delivery of the Degree programme. This paved the path for the new Faculty of Engineering to build enduring relationships with the industry. Together with the inputs from the CCE and the Industry, a proposal was formulated to be formally submitted to the University Grants Commission. The University Grants Commission approved the proposal to establish a new Faculty of Engineering at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura in December 2015. The new Faculty along with its Departments of Study, was gazetted by the government in January 2016. 10

The University of Sri Jayewardenepura acquired a 10-acre land in Mattegoda, Kottawa, for the establishment of the Faculty of Engineering on the 31st of July 2017. The acquired land is located very close to the buzzing and growing city center of Kottawa, which makes it easily accessible through the Southern Highway as well as a multitude of road networks. The land allocation was supported through the 2019 National Budget, with an investment of Rs. 1 billion. This was a momentous occasion for the faculty, which is the youngest state-owned Engineering Faculty in Sri Lanka. 11

Since the groundbreaking ceremony of the proposed Faculty of Engineering building complex was held on 31st December 2020, a major milestone in the faculty’s journey is its relocation to a state-of-the-art permanent complex in Kottawa (Mattegoda). The new complex has been designed to accommodate up to 1,600 students and to provide an exceptional learning environment that supports academic excellence, innovation, and student well-being. Equipped with cutting-edge technology and advanced infrastructure, the new faculty complex features modern modular laboratories that facilitate hands-on experimentation, innovation, and research. A fully equipped 800-seat auditorium serves as a central venue for academic events, conferences, ceremonies, and student showcases. To ensure student and staff well-being and convenience, the premises also include a spacious food court, recreational facilities such as a badminton court and gymnasium, and a dedicated daycare centre, enhancing accessibility and inclusivity for staff and students with families. 12

section: Beyond the Classroom: A Holistic Campus Life
text: What sets this facility apart, however, is its attention to the human element of engineering. Recognizing that innovation requires well-being, the designers have integrated features rarely seen in state university faculties. Details from the faculty’s profile reveal a campus built for life, not just study. The new Engineering Faculty Library has been transformed into a vibrant hub with self-check kiosks and security gates, designed to make resources instantly accessible. It offers spacious reading areas and relaxing leisure spaces, a deliberate move to foster collaborative learning over rote memorization. The student experience is further bolstered by dedicated recreational facilities, an E-learning and language center, a career guidance unit, and an industrial training unit. The complex includes an indoor sports complex and a fully equipped gymnasium, ensuring students can balance the rigors of engineering with physical health. An open-air amphitheater provides a space for cultural events, while a modern food court and multiple canteens offer high-quality amenities for social interaction. The addition of a dedicated daycare center, alongside a health center and pharmacy, underscores the faculty’s commitment to supporting the diverse needs of its community, particularly those with families. Accessibility is a key priority, with the premises offering substantial parking capacity to ensure hassle-free access for the university community. 13

The Faculty of Engineering is deeply committed to research, innovation, and industry collaboration. With a clear vision of becoming a Future Engineering Research Hub, the faculty fosters practice-oriented research and encourages students to develop real-world solutions to contemporary engineering and societal challenges. Under the guidance of a dedicated and dynamic academic staff, students actively participate in national and international competitions and have already secured multiple awards, an impressive achievement for the youngest state-owned engineering faculty in the country. The Faculty is initiating collaborations with industry to produce young Engineers to fit the contemporary needs of the Engineering sector of the country, which is essential for continuing national development. Research Committee of the Faculty of Engineering (RCFE) has been established to facilitate research and innovation activities. The faculty currently has students following Mphil and PhD degrees related to the specialisations of all four academic departments.

The Faculty actively takes measures to improve the academic standards to align with international quality standards. This process is facilitated by the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) of the Faculty. IQAC is responsible for carrying out and coordinating quality assurance activities of the Faculty in line with national and international standards for an engineering degree program, namely the Sri Lanka Qualification Framework (SLQF) and the Washington Accord of the International Engineering Alliance, for which the IESL is the authorized organization for the accreditation.

All the degree programs offered by the Faculty of Engineering, University of Sri Jayewardenepura have obtained the IESL recognition; Civil Engineering and Mechanical Engineering departments are fully recognized, and working towards obtaining the IESL accreditation. 15

Continuous Assessment(CA) has been introduced for every Course in order to maintain the motivation in the learning process as well as to guide the student towards achieving the learning outcomes. This consists of components such as mid semester examinations, practical work, fieldwork, assignments, quizzes, and mini projects, which evaluate the performance of a student throughout the semester. Components of CA vary from Course to Course depending on the nature of the Course. The aggregate mark derived from different components of CA is referred to as the Continuous Assessment Mark (CA Mark).
End of Semester Examination (ESE) is the final assessment component of a Course , which is conducted at the end of each semester.

Overall Assessment Mark (OA Mark) is computed by combining both the CA Mark and the ESE Mark according to a pre-defined relationship, which may differ from Course to Course. The OA Mark determines the academic standing of the student in the Course.

Compulsory Course Requirements (CCR), if any, need to be satisfied in order to sit the ESE of the Course. These requirements may include successfully completing the prescribed CA components, attendance at lectures, etc. This information will be made available to the students prior to the commencement of academic activities.

section: Re-sitting the ESE of a Course
text: A student is required to re-sit the ESE without following the Course in full if, a. CA Mark is above the pass mark, and b. OA Mark is below the pass mark. In such cases, the CA Mark may be brought forward while the best grade obtainable by the student is limited to ‘C’.

A student has to repeat a Course if, a. both the CA Mark and the OA Mark are below the pass mark, or b. CCR is not satisfied, hence not permitted to sit the ESE. In this case, the student has to follow the Course in full. This implies that the student must satisfy the CCR and successfully complete the CA Component and the ESE. The best grade obtainable by repeating a Course is limited to ‘C’.

A student is permitted to postpone academic activities of a Course for a valid reason, subject to the approval of the Faculty Board and the Senate. Such permission, if granted, is known as an Academic Concession. A student who has been granted an Academic Concession is required to fulfil the requirements of the Course, as applicable, in the subsequent academic year.
A Learning Management System (LMS) is a software application used to facilitate e-learning in the delivery of the Courses. 20

Selection of students to one of the four fields of specialization will take place at the end of the second semester. The selection process is strictly based on the preference and performance of the students during the first two semesters.

A student has the option to claim for a ‘Minor’ relevant to his field of specialization after successfully completing an approved combination of Courses. Students will be made aware of such Courses in advance. Minors on offer include emerging fields of Engineering such as ‘Biomedical Engineering’, ‘Building Services Engineering’, ‘Environmental Engineering’, ‘Mechatronics Engineering’ and ‘Data Management’, and may vary from time to time, as determined by the Faculty Board.

With the aim of producing knowledgeable, competent, confident, and innovative engineering graduates, the curriculum offered at the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura has been carefully designed by distinguished academics and industry partners to comply with the international standard for engineering programmes, namely the Washington Accord of the International Engineering Alliance. During the first year of the degree programme, every student should follow a common curriculum to acquire basic knowledge in engineering and be prepared to select a suitable field of specialization at the end of the first semester. In the subsequent semesters, students should follow compulsory courses of the selected specialization. Additionally, the students continue to follow courses in Mathematics, English, and complementary interdisciplinary study areas, and will undergo Industrial Training that aligns with their specialized field of study. Students will also have the opportunity to obtain a minor within their specialized stream by taking elective courses in respective streams in the third and fourth years of the degree programme. Further, in the fourth year (the final two semesters), students will undertake a major engineering/research project in their field of specialization.
The common curriculum consists of preliminary courses in Engineering, Mathematics, History, and English communication and presentation skills.

Civil Engineering specializes in a broad spectrum of engineering aspects, including envisioning, planning, designing and construction of buildings, highways and bridges, reservoirs, dams and irrigation schemes, power houses and transmission systems, water supply and sewerage schemes, tunnels and underground structures, and so on. The graduates can choose from a wide range of opportunities in industry and consulting practices as well as in research and development, which has both local and global significance. They also would have the option of pursuing an academic career combined with research, innovation, and development work among local and international research communities. Amongst its many courses, the Department of Civil Engineering offers subjects that cover the key specialization areas in Civil Engineering, such as Structural, Geotechnical, Transportation and Highways, Hydraulics, and Environmental Engineering, while bestowing an in-depth knowledge in Sustainable Designs, Construction Technology, and management as well as Surveying. The Department of Computer Engineering offers courses to undergraduates from fundamentals to complex and advanced topics in modern computer engineering such as computer hardware and embedded system design, software engineering, bioinformatics, artificial intelligence, computer vision, robotics, parallel computing, networking, computer security, cloud computing, and database systems. Minor speciality areas such as Data Management and High-Performance Computing have been introduced with the degree programme. Students who follow Data Management shall explore the topics of natural language processing, quality engineering, and machine learning, where it integrates current data science research and data-analytic techniques to find solutions in various domains. Students who follow High-Performance Computing shall study topics such as cloud computing and applications, advanced computer architecture, and GPU programming. Students will be able to gain experience in those areas by involving in multiple projects. With the knowledge and skills gained, a Computer Engineering undergraduate will be provided with countless opportunities to work in the industry as a Computer Engineer, System Design Engineer, System Architect, Software Engineer, or can continue onto postgraduate studies and research.

The Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering offers a specialization that spans all scales of Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Electrical and Electronics Engineering graduates are in high demand in the industry and academia, both locally and internationally, in a multitude of areas including electronic designing and manufacturing, power generation, industrial and power electronics, automation systems, computer programming, telecommunications, robotics, health care, manufacturing, and water and energy systems.

The courses offered by the Department of Mechanical Engineering are designed to give students the broad skill set required to pursue their goals, whether that is working as a Mechanical Engineer, Product Design Engineer, Energy Consultant, Entrepreneur, or continuing on to graduate study and research, throughout the globe. This specialization combines a broad-based education in the engineering sciences with a strong grounding in quantitative, problem solving, design, and communication skills. In the Department of Mechanical Engineering, students learn by doing, experiencing a level of understanding that only occurs through creative activities. The department offers minors in areas of emerging sciences in Mechanical Engineering. Currently the minors in Mechatronics, Building Services and Manufacturing Engineering are offered by the department. The minor in Mechatronics Engineering covers the areas of robotics, vision systems, control systems, advanced automation, and micro mechatronics. The minor in Manufacturing Engineering covers the areas of production and operations management, advanced manufacturing systems and computer aided designing and manufacturing. Heating,ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, piped services and green building engineering are covered in the minor of Building Services. The curriculum of Mechanical Engineering ranges across the fundamentals of engineering mechanics, thermodynamics, energy engineering, building services, manufacturing, aerodynamics, and computer- based simulations with numerical approaches to designing products with a significant impact to society.

Each student registered to follow the Degree Programme in Engineering will be issued with a Student Record Book (SRB) by the University. The SRB must be updated as the student progresses in the study programme. This book contains basic information of the student, such as his name, registration number, date of registration, contact information, and national identity card number. The SRB is the property of the University and should not be abused, altered and tampered with or transferred to a third party. In the event of the loss of the SRB, a student should immediately report the loss to the Students Affairs Division/ Dean of the Faculty. In the event a duplicate SRB is to be issued, the student concerned will be liable to pay a surcharge and the cost of issuing the record book.

All students are provided with an Identity Card issued by the University. Each student is required to carry the Identity Card in person at all times within the University premises. Student should produce the Identity Card and prove his identity on being asked to do so by any Academic Staff member, security personnel or any other person authorized to do so by the Vice Chancellor. The Identity Card is the property of the University and should not be abused, altered and tampered with or transferred to a third party. In the event of the loss of the Identity Card, the student should immediately report the loss to the Students Affairs Division/ Dean of the Faculty. The student concerned will be liable to pay a surcharge and the cost of issuing a duplicate Identity Card.

Students are expected to behave responsibly without disrupting activities of the faculty. In case a student behaves otherwise, he/she may be subjected to disciplinary action by the University in accordance with the ‘By-laws on Student Discipline’. All students must be aware of the provisions in the “Prohibition of Ragging and Other Forms of Violence in Educational Institutions Act, No. 20 of 1998”. 73

section: Policy on Excusing from Academic Activities
text: A student may be excused from academic activities such as lectures, tutorials, practical work, and assignments due to the demise of a parent, a sibling, or spouse, or due to any valid medical reason. The student is responsible for submitting authentic evidence, within fourteen (14) days of the event due to which ‘excuse’ is being sought. The acceptability of such evidence would be determined by the Faculty.

The procedure a student should follow during examinations are described in the “Examination criteria, rules and regulations, examination irregularities, punishments applicable to candidates sitting first degrees, postgraduate degrees and external degrees conducted by the University” in Student Handbook of University of Sri Jayewardenepura. Violation of the provisions described in the document under reference, will result in the student being disciplinarily dealt with. All students are required to educate themselves about the examination procedure and the respective Rules and Regulations of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura.

Mahapola scholarships are awarded to selected students based on merit or need where they would receive financial assistance as determined by the Mahapola Trust Fund. Students are informed via public notice by the Welfare Division about the dates on which the instalments will be paid.

Those who are not eligible for the Mahapola scholarship may apply for University Bursaries for financial assistance. Further information will be available with the Welfare Division of the University, who will receive and process the applications.

The Library plays an important role in the university’s education, supporting the three main pillars of the university: teaching, learning, and research. In the Main Library of the Sri Jayewardenepura University, there is a collection of more than two hundred thousand books, and hundreds of journals and electronic databases. The library has acquired a number of electronic resources such as e-books, e-journals, bibliographies and full text databases covering varieties of subject areas. All these databases and free sources are listed under e-resources in the library website. 74
Students from the Faculty of Engineering can use both the Main Library located within the main campus premises and the branch Faculty Library located within the Engineering Faculty premises.

section: Library of the Faculty of Engineering
text: The library of the Faculty of Engineering contains all the relevant textbooks in the four major disciplinary streams of Engineering along with supportive subject areas and other relevant reading materials. Students could also use the computers in the Faculty Library to access electronic databases and journals. The usual opening hours of the library are from 8.15 am to 4.15 pm on weekdays. However, opening hours could be extended based on special requirements. 75

The Industrial Training Division (ITD) of the Faculty of Engineering, University of Sri Jayewardenepura is functioning directly under the Dean of the Faculty of Engineering and is located at the Faculty of Engineering, Lumbini Avenue, Ratmalana. Students following the Bachelor of Science of Engineering Honours degree conducted by the Faculty of Engineering, University of Sri Jayewardenepura are required to undergo 24 weeks of industrial training in an industrial establishment as a compulsory requirement of the study programme. The ITD in collaboration with the respective departments of the Faculty and the National Apprentice and Industrial Training Authority (NAITA) make arrangements to place the students in suitable establishments for idustrial training. The ITD is also responsible for managing and monitoring matters related to industrial training, coordinating with training providers, supervising the students during training and conducting assessments.

The students could access the Computer Center of the Faculty of Engineering, which is equipped with modern computers that are networked and provided with internet facilities. The Computer Centre is equipped to facilitate both the first-year common courses and some of the courses taken under specialized streams. All students will be provided with a university student email account upon request. Free Wi-Fi is available within the faculty premises to all the students. 76

The faculty canteen provides cooked meals, hot/cold beverages, and other food items for the students at concession rates. The Convenience Store offers products such as confectioneries, snacks, cold beverages, stationary items, printed media, and other daily commodities. A photocopy service is also available at the Convenience Store.

Separate hostel accommodation is available for both male and female students of the faculty. The priority is given to first year and fourth year students. Since accommodation in hostels is limited, please be noted that university authorities may not be able to provide accommodation to all applicants.

Each student is assigned with an academic staff member as his/her mentor to support smooth engagement in academic activities. Students are encouraged to discuss the academic/personal issues that hinder his/her studies with the assigned mentor. 77 77

As provided in the Universities Act No. 16 of 1978 and as amended, there exist University Student Council, Faculty Unions and other societies, which function under By-laws approved by the University. Further, there is a multitude of University approved learned societies, which will engage students in religious, educational and recreational activities.

IESL Student Chapter in the University of Sri Jayewardenepura is one of the most active student chapters which is established in collaboration with the IESL Young Members’ Section. The objectives of the chapter are to disseminate knowledge, theory and practice of aspects related to the relevant discipline of engineering while professionally developing the students and encouraging them to be socially responsible people. The initial foundation for the Chapter was laid by Dr. Akila Subasinghe, the founding Dean of the Faculty and Dr. Chamitha de Alwis in 2017. The formal establishment of the IESL Student Chapter took place on 9th of September 2019 under the guidance of Prof. K.M.C. Konthesingha and Dr. G.N. Samarasekara. Since the establishment, the chapter has been actively incorporating with the faculty undergraduates by supplementing them with educational, professional and soft skills development activities to help them to mold themselves into skilled engineers. The chapter’s activities include seminars focusing on various disciplines of engineering and soft skill development, webinars with the cooperation of academics and industry experts, CSR projects, activities with the cooperation of IESL Sri Lanka, etc. All the undergraduate and postgraduate students of the Faculty of Engineering are eligible to be members of the IESL Student Chapter. The students can take part in various activities and events such as IESL day, IESL Techno, Techno Games, IESL YMS Technical Conference, Inter University Debate Competition, Talk to School programs which are conducted in collaboration with the IESL, Sri Lanka.

The Institution of Engineering & Technology (IET) is one of the premier professional engineering organizations in Sri Lanka with headquarters in the UK. As a professional organization, IET plays a major role in the career development of engineering professionals throughout the world. IET global network has a membership of over 167,000 qualified engineers representing 150 countries over the world gaining support and recognition from the IET. The IET Sri Lanka is the 9th local network in the South Asian region and it has been set up to serve the members of IET who live in Sri Lanka and to coordinate local activities. The local network’s activities include evening forums, committee meetings, technical sessions, workshops, international conferences/symposiums, field visits, conducting radio/TV programs for public awareness, and younger member sessions. The IET has had members in Sri Lanka for over 80 years, with a current growing membership of over 1,000 engineers. IET Sri Lanka collaborates with the Institution of Engineers Sri Lanka (IESL), the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), the British Computer Society (BCS), the Computer Society of Sri Lanka (CSSL), the Institute of Physics Sri Lanka (IPSL) and the engineering faculties of the universities in Sri Lanka for many activities in the electrical, electronics & telecommunications and computer engineering related fields.

The IET Young Professionals Sri Lanka Network (IET YP SLN) consists of young IET members who are below the age of 35 and student members (undergraduates). The Young Woman Engineer (YWE) Award, which was initiated in 2017, is the key event of the YP SLN. Apart from that, several workshops, guest lectures, competitions, technical conferences, and field visits are organized for the younger members and undergraduate students. Annually, the Young Professional Technical Conference (YPTC) is organized for students to showcase their research works. IET YP SLN supports students to build a community as a society or student organization within the university by providing resources and funding for extracurricular events. Under the IET YP SLN, there are nine on-campus. The IET On-Campus at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura is the 8th one that was initiated in 2022, and in that short period too, it was awarded the Best IET On-Campus in that year.

IEEE, founded in 1884, stands as the world’s largest technical professional society, born during a transformative era when electricity was reshaping society. Visionaries like Alexander Graham Bell and Thomas Edison were early contributors. In 1963, the merger of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers (AIEE) and the Institute of Radio Engineers (IRE) gave rise to IEEE, now connecting brilliant minds across diverse fields to advance science and technology for humanity's benefit.

section: The IEEE Student Branch at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, part of
text: IEEE Sri Lanka Section, was established in 2018 under the leadership of Mr. Dulan Dias. It aims to advance technology and professionalism, offering educational, technical, and professional advantages to its members. Notably, in 2022, the branch earned the IEEE Regional Exemplary Student Branch Award, led by current Chairperson Ms. Wasana Shalini and Branch Counselor Prof. Lasith Gunawardena. Dedicated to fostering connections, our branch hosts various events to promote community and collaboration among members and with other branches. From the Annual General Meeting (AGM) to celebrating IEEE Day, our focus is on showcasing IEEE's importance, enticing new members, and encouraging active involvement. JamborIEEE camps unite multiple SBs, enhancing inter-branch connections, while initiatives like Road to Legacy guide first-year IT undergraduates. J’Pura Expedition 2024 featured tech talks by esteemed speakers, spanning AI to robotics, providing insights into cutting-edge technologies. With an exciting event lineup ahead, we remain committed to our mission of fostering connections and creating memorable experiences. Join us on this journey of learning, growth, and community-building within the IEEE Student Branch. 80

The Civil Engineering Society (CES) is the main society within the Department of Civil Engineering that consists of the academic staff, undergraduate and postgraduate students. The society has been established with broader aims of promoting the civil engineering profession among students, enhancing the networking opportunities among the members and with the wider civil engineering community, promoting the professional development of students, and improving the student’s life in the department. Apart, CES represents the department in inter-university, national, and international Level activities including IESL TECHNO exhibitions and design competitions. Intra university level spaghetti bridge competitions are organized by the CES annually. In addition, the society organizes guest lectures by inviting key personnel from the industry and research organizations. Apart from the activities related to the Civil Engineering field CES promote and encourage students to serve underprivileged sectors of the society. 81

Computer Engineering Society (CENSOC) of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura was established as the main society of the Department of Computer Engineering. Membership of CENSOC is open to all undergraduate and postgraduate students and academic/ academic support/ technical staff attached to the Department of Computer Engineering. CENSOC aims to establish interaction among members and to promote professional interest in the field of Computer Engineering. The society explores and provides opportunities to fulfill its societal responsibilities to the community. Further, CENSOC will act as the social arm that identifies inherent capabilities of students and promote their leadership skills and professionalism. 82

Electrical and Electronic Engineering Club (E Club) of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura is the prestigious social arm of the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Membership of E Club is open to all undergraduate/postgraduate students and members of the academic/academic support/technical staff attached to the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering. 2

E Club promotes professional interest in the area of Electrical and Electronic Engineering and establishes closer interactions among members. The club intend to inspire its members towards personal and societal developments as applicable to Electrical and Electronic Engineering. The activities of the E Club include, but not limited to, organizing guest talks, presentations, field visits, workshops, competitions, carrier fairs, fun activities and charity projects. 2 2 2 83 2

section: IMechE - University of Sri Jayewardenepura Student Chapter
text: The Institution of Mechanical Engineers (IMechE) Student Chapter of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, established in December 2019, is dedicated to promoting the significance of mechanical engineering through various innovative initiatives. In addition to organizing sessions featuring keynote speeches and engaging panel discussions to underscore the importance of the field, the chapter actively fosters hands-on learning experiences. Annually, the chapter participates to the Speak Out for Engineers (SOFE) competition, providing a dynamic platform for students to showcase their talents and innovative ideas. Moreover, recognizing the importance of practical exposure, the chapter collaborates with industry experts to conduct specialized sessions covering key areas of the engineering profession. These sessions offer invaluable insights, practical skills, and networking opportunities, enriching the academic journey of its members and preparing them for the challenges of the professional world. 84

The Mechanical Engineering Members Society (MEMS) at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (USJ) is dedicated to creating a collaborative community within the Department of Mechanical Engineering. MEMS aims to exchange experiences and knowledge among students, staff, and alumni, and enhance industrial collaborations for career guidance. The society organizes competitions, exhibitions, and events to showcase outstanding projects and skills, and seeks affiliations with other universities and research institutes. MEMS also contributes to professional development and research advancement through workshops and seminars. The society is committed to public outreach, uplifting the local community, and supporting department initiatives. Recent endeavors, such as hosting the Stream-Xtream computational fluid dynamics (CFD) competition at Techno 2023, demonstrate MEMS' dedication to enriching the academic experience for its members. 85

The NEXUS Club of University of Sri Jayewardenepura was established in October 2023, with the aim of fostering unity, promoting team building, and nurturing leadership qualities among students. It serves as a platform to enrich aesthetic appreciation by encouraging engagement in various creative pursuits such as music, dancing, drama, photography, and exploratory activities. Additionally, the club is dedicated to enhancing language and communication skills, fostering personality development, and facilitating interdisciplinary discussions related to engineering. NEXUS Club is open to all students across the four departments, and serves as a nexus, interconnecting individuals from diverse academic backgrounds and providing a supportive environment for personal and intellectual growth. Join the Nexus Club in the journey of exploration, creativity, and collaboration as we strive to cultivate well-rounded individuals equipped with the skills and mindset to excel both academically and beyond.

The Career Guidance Unit of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura offers assistance to students in developing skills that would shape them to be productive in the local and international industry. Career Guidance Cell (CGC-FoE) of Faculty of Engineering was established under the purview of the Career Guidance Unit of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura. The CGC-FoE aims to support undergraduates in acquiring attributes and soft skills which can assist them in reaching standards matching the potential employer’s requirements. The cell comprises of academic career advisors from each department and an experienced career guidance counselor as a career advisor. http://eng.sjp.ac.lk/career-guidance-center/ 87 Career Guidance Society is the student club of the Career Guidance Cell of the Faculty of Engineering. Students can join the society upon registration, where they can get the exposure to various acitvities organized by the society, to enhance their knowledge,, and skills and develop the career path, from the early stages of the undargraduate studies. The society organizes several workshops, seminars and welfare programmes, having these objectives in mind. Further, as the main event of the society, a career fair, followed by a workshop series are organized anually, to connect employers with the undergraduate students, to facilitate with career opportunities.

Sports and recreational activities of the university are managed by the Department of Physical Education. The Department of Physical Education provides an opportunity for students to take part in different recreational and sports activities and to develop personalities and qualities of teamwork through such participation. The students may also enjoy a game of carom and badminton within the faculty premises. The Engineering faculty medical center caters to the university community including students, staff and their families free of charge as the first contact and coordinate with Colombo South Teaching Hospital for secondary care. The medical center provides facilities for students and staff during the daytime. Other medical facilities such as, preventive health care (Dengue control program), ambulance facilities, dental facilities, etc. are provided by the main medical center of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura. The Counselling Center of the Faculty of Engineering offers counselling services to the students of the faculty to maintain their mental well-being. http://eng.sjp.ac.lk/medical-center/
